To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
remuneration in financial services sector in the UK is determined by the organizational form, size and performance.

the determinants of the remuneration of executive directors of demutualised societies are different from those of the remunation of executive directors of traditional building societies, traditional retail banks and the pre-demutualisation positions of the demutualised companies; the determinants of executives remuneration changed after demutalization; the relationships between remueration and size disappeared; remuneration committees of demutualization societies use industry norms to attract executives irrespective of performance.
the determinants and the role of determinants changed after the demutualization of building societies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determinants of CEO remuneration in UK financial institutions.
the determinants of CEO compensation in the financial services sector, which has recently been subject to a series of corporate governance scandals.
the impact of organizational form on the remuneration of executives in the UK financial sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the determinants have changed in a way that is not in line with the expectations of the remuneration committees and the regulators, and that this is likely to be detrimental to the long-term performance of the demutualized organizations.
the demutualized financial institutions have become more similar to their plc competitors.
the determinants have changed in the UK financial sector after demutualizations, and this has been reflected in the remuneration packages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the determinants and the level of executive remunera-tion in demutualized companies differ from the pre-demutualized positions and from the traditional retail and mutual banks.
the remuneration of executives in the financial services sector is determined by the industry, and not the performance of the firm.
the remuneration committees are not able to use the remuneration as a tool to attract, retain, and motivate executives in the UK financial sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UK government should reconsider the remuneration regulations in the financial sector, as the current regulations do not seem to be effective.
the remuneration of the executives of demutualization companies is driven by the industry norms, which is not the case in traditional retail banks and building societies.
the determinants are different in mutual and plc organizations and the role of the determinant changed after demuturalization.
